title: Property-tax design reallocates housing access across generations under financial constraints
source_unit: NBER Working Paper 35587, overlapping-generations model of property taxation, housing allocation, and financial constraints
geography: United States housing policy with a California-to-Texas property-tax counterfactual; intergenerational housing allocation

observations.period: Paper issued August 10, 2026; model counterfactual for California property taxes and housing tenure

denominator.unit: overlapping-generations housing-allocation model and California-to-Texas tax-rate counterfactual

property_tax_rate_counterfactual.unit: California property-tax rate raised to Texas-level rate in the model

house_price_change.unit: modeled California house-price change under the counterfactual

older_homeownership_change.unit: modeled change in homeownership among adults age 75 and older

allocation_mechanism.unit: lower capitalized prices reduce downpayments for constrained young buyers; higher tax obligations raise older owners' holding costs

step_up_basis.unit: modeled housing-tenure response to a tax-treatment change

observations.method: Overlapping-generations model with financially constrained households, housing capitalization, property-tax obligations, and tax treatment of bequests; California-to-Texas rate counterfactual and step-up-basis counterfactual.
observations.uncertainty: These are model-generated counterfactuals rather than observed policy effects from a California tax reform. Results depend on the model's demographic, financial-constraint, housing-supply, tax-incidence, and bequest assumptions; the abstract does not establish neighborhood displacement, rental effects, service quality, or actual political feasibility.
observations.subgroup: Young financially constrained prospective homeowners, older homeowners, and households whose housing tenure is affected by property-tax and bequest-tax treatment; age groups and tenure states are not interchangeable.
observations.counterinterpretation: Higher property taxes can reduce prices and help some constrained buyers while imposing higher holding costs on existing owners. Supply responses, rental-market adjustment, exemptions, local public-service benefits, mobility, family transfers, and political resistance could alter the modeled incidence.

related_sources.claim: Official NBER DOI identifies the working paper.

boundary: This record establishes a modeled intergenerational housing-allocation mechanism. It does not establish an observed California policy effect, individual displacement, rental burden, local-service change, household wealth change, or political response.
